security_audit.summary: Seven command findings are confirmed because the setup guide recommends package execution, schema generation, migrations, or tool configuration changes. The other 63 detections are Markdown formatting, safe examples, or official reference links with no automatic execution or exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The guide uses mutable or unpinned npx package versions for executable CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed CLI versions and require explicit user confirmation before package installation, schema generation, migrations, or MCP configuration changes.

remediation.issue: Migration and database push commands can alter persistent state without a documented preview or backup step.
remediation.suggestion: Require target verification, migration review, and a current backup before applying schema changes outside disposable development databases.

content.value_statement: Authentication setup often fails through mismatched adapters, session storage, plugins, or environment settings. This skill provides focused Better Auth configuration and security guidance.
actual_capabilities: Outlines Better Auth server and client setup workflows.
Explains direct database connections and Prisma, Drizzle, and MongoDB adapters.
Describes session storage priority, cookie cache strategies, and invalidation options.
Lists email, OAuth, plugin, hook, and rate limiting configuration points.
Highlights secure cookies, trusted origins, CSRF checks, and origin checks.
Identifies common model naming, schema generation, and Drizzle configuration errors.
limitations: It is a reference guide and does not inspect an application automatically.
It does not replace current Better Auth documentation or release notes.
It does not validate database credentials, provider settings, or deployment infrastructure.
Its migration commands can change files or database state and require user approval.

use_cases.title: Start TypeScript Authentication
use_cases.description: Plan a Better Auth server, client, route handler, environment variables, and initial database schema.

use_cases.title: Review Session Security
use_cases.description: Assess storage priority, cookie strategy, secure cookies, trusted origins, and rate limiting before deployment.

use_cases.title: Integrate Database Adapters
use_cases.description: Choose and configure a direct driver, Prisma, Drizzle, or MongoDB adapter while avoiding model naming errors.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a basic Better Auth setup for my TypeScript application with email and password authentication.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting authentication in a new application.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Drizzle
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Better Auth with Drizzle and PostgreSQL, including environment variables, adapter setup, schema generation, and a development migration workflow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when connecting Better Auth to an existing Drizzle project.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Session Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Better Auth session configuration for storage priority, cookie caching, secure cookies, trusted origins, and rate limiting.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Better Auth architecture with secondary storage, OAuth, two-factor authentication, hooks, and typed clients. Identify migration and security risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a complex application with separate client and server projects.

output_examples.input: Plan Better Auth with PostgreSQL and email authentication.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering secrets, base URL, database connection, email settings, route mounting, schema generation, migration review, and health verification.

output_examples.input: Review a stateless session design using cookie caching.
output: Explains that session data remains in the cookie without a database.
Compares compact, signed JWT, and encrypted JWE strategies.
Flags cache expiry, custom field refresh, secure cookie, and global invalidation considerations.

best_practices: Confirm package installation and migration commands before execution.
Keep secrets in environment variables and use secure cookies in production.
Recheck current documentation and regenerate schemas after plugin changes.
anti_patterns: Do not disable CSRF or origin checks without a documented security review.
Do not use database table names where an adapter expects model names.
Do not apply generated migrations to production without reviewing targets, changes, and backups.

faq.question: Does this skill install Better Auth automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and guidance, but package installation and migrations require explicit approval.

faq.question: Which database adapters are covered?
faq.answer: It covers direct database drivers and Better Auth adapters for Drizzle, Prisma, and MongoDB.

faq.question: Can it help with stateless sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cookie caching, storage priority, signed and encrypted strategies, expiry, and invalidation.

faq.question: Does it cover OAuth and plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies social provider configuration, common plugins, dedicated import paths, and matching client plugins.

faq.question: Does it replace the official documentation?
faq.answer: No. Better Auth APIs can change, so current official documentation remains authoritative.

faq.question: What security settings does it highlight?
faq.answer: It covers secure cookies, trusted origins, CSRF checks, origin checks, cross-subdomain cookies, proxy headers, and rate limiting.
